title: paper-research: usage and security

options.content: **How to read this.** Claude Code sends one event per prompt, model call, tool call, hook, and so on. Use the time picker above. Each row has its own help, and every panel queries on its own, so an empty panel doesn't affect the others. Hover the **i** in a panel's corner for what it counts. An empty panel usually means that event hasn't happened in the range. The links above open the other two dashboards.

Totals for the time range, for every Claude Code session that sends telemetry here. **Cost** adds up every model call. A **skill run** is one use of a paper-research skill; a **script run** is a Bash call that ran one of its scripts. Per-prompt numbers follow the **Model call source** box above.

panels.title: Risky commands
panels.description: Shell calls that mention curl, wget, ssh, sudo, rm -rf, .env, credentials, and similar. Code that sends data out from a script, such as python -c with urllib, is not matched, so a zero is not proof of no network access.

targets.expr: sum(count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name=~"Bash|PowerShell" | line_format `{{.tool_parameters}}` | json | full_command=~`(?is).*((^|[\s;&|(=/\\"'\x60])(sudo|curl|wget|ssh|scp|nc|ncat|chmod|base64|iwr|Invoke-WebRequest)([.]exe)?($|[\s;&|)"'\x60])|rm\s+(-[a-z]+\s+)*-[a-z]*(rf|fr)|rm\s+-[a-z]*r[a-z]*\s+(-[a-z]+\s+)*-[a-z]*f|rm\s+-[a-z]*f[a-z]*\s+(-[a-z]+\s+)*-[a-z]*r|Remove-Item\b[^;&|\n]*-Recurse|(^|[\s/\\"'=~])([.]env([.](local|production|prod|development|dev|staging|test))?|[.]ssh|credentials|id_rsa|id_ed25519)($|[\s"'/\\;|&])).*` [$__range])) or vector(0)

options.content: What the plugin did, as Claude Code recorded it, so it works with the debug log off. A **skill run** is one use of a paper-research skill (`/read`, `/add`, and so on). A **script run** is a Bash call that ran one of its scripts. Claude Code doesn't time a skill alone, so a skill gets the time and cost of the prompt it ran in, shared with any other skill in that prompt.

panels.title: Time and cost per skill
panels.description: For each skill: runs, the cost of the prompts they ran in, and those prompts' time (model calls plus tools) as total, p50, p90 and max. Claude and Plugin scripts split the total. With fewer than about 10 runs, p90 is the max. The numbers are approximate: a prompt that ran two skills counts in full for each, so the rows add up to more than the real cost and time.

targets.expr: sum by (prompt_id) (sum_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name=~"Bash|PowerShell" | tool_parameters=~`.*scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py.*` | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]))

panels.title: Skill runs
panels.description: One row per skill run, longest first: the time of its prompt split into model calls and tools, and the prompt's cost. Search the Events log on the service dashboard for the prompt id to follow it.

panels.title: Scripts
panels.description: Each plugin script: how often Claude ran it, how often it failed, and how long a run took. A call that runs two scripts counts for the first.

targets.expr: sum by (script) (count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name=~"Bash|PowerShell" | tool_parameters=~`.*scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py.*` | line_format `{{.tool_parameters}}` | regexp `scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(?P<script>arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py` [$__range]))

sum by (script) (count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name=~"Bash|PowerShell" | tool_parameters=~`.*scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py.*` | line_format `{{.tool_parameters}}` | regexp `scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(?P<script>arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py` | success="false" [$__range]))

avg by (script) (avg_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name=~"Bash|PowerShell" | tool_parameters=~`.*scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py.*` | line_format `{{.tool_parameters}}` | regexp `scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(?P<script>arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py` | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]))

max by (script) (max_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_result" | tool_name=~"Bash|PowerShell" | tool_parameters=~`.*scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py.*` | line_format `{{.tool_parameters}}` | regexp `scripts[^a-z0-9_]{1,4}(?P<script>arxiv|s2|graph|init|recap|debuglog)[.]py` | unwrap duration_ms [$__range]))

panels.title: Plugin versions
panels.description: Sessions in which a paper-research skill ran, by the plugin version that was loaded, with their skill runs and script runs, to compare releases. Cost is the whole session's, including work that did not use the plugin, so read it as a rough guide. A session that started before the time range has no load event in it and is left out.

options.content: Every model call carries the `prompt_id` of the prompt that caused it, so a prompt's cost is the sum of its calls. Background calls (session titles, suggestions, compaction) are included; narrow them with **Model call source** above, where `sdk` is the main conversation.

panels.title: Most expensive prompts
panels.description: The ten costliest prompts, with their model calls and the paper-research skills that ran in them.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (prompt_id) (sum_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="api_request" | prompt_id!="" | query_source=~"$query_source" | unwrap cost_usd [$__range])))

options.content: Signs of something unexpected: rejected calls, hooks that block, risky shell commands, sensitive files, MCP servers you didn't add, and pages fetched. These panels show tool inputs, which can hold secrets, so keep the stack on this machine only (it listens on 127.0.0.1). The plugin's own guard decisions and hosts are on the debug log dashboard.

panels.title: Tool decisions
panels.description: Who decided each tool call: config (a rule or auto mode), user, or hook. In auto mode, Classifier is the classifier's verdict. A rise of accept by config can mean a rule was loosened.

targets.expr: sum by (decision, source, permission_mode, classifier_verdict) (count_over_time({service_name="claude-code"} | event_name="tool_decision" [$__range]))

defaults.noValue: No data in this time range
